chunks.arabic_text: وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:

translations.en: And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:

chunks.arabic_text: «لَا أُلْفِيَنَّ مِنْكُمْ رَجُلًا مَاتَ لَهُ مَيِّتٌ لَيْلًا فَانْتَظَرَ بِهِ الصُّبْحَ وَ لَا رَجُلًا مَاتَ لَهُ مَيِّتٌ نَهَارًا فَانْتَظَرَ بِهِ اللَّيْلَ لَا تَنْتَظِرُوا بِمَوْتَاكُمْ طُلُوعَ الشَّمْسِ وَ لَا غُرُوبَهَا عَجِّلُوا بِهِمْ إِلَى مَضَاجِعِهِمْ يَرْحَمُكُمُ اللَّهُ»

translations.en: "I do not want to find among you a man whose deceased died at night and he waited with him until morning, nor a man whose deceased died by day and he waited with him until night. Do not wait with your dead for the rising of the sun or its setting. Hasten them to their resting places; may Allah have mercy on you."

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ النَّاسُ وَ أَنْتَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ.

translations.en: So the people said: "And you also, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah have mercy on you."

en.summary: This hadith instructs the believers not to delay the burial of the deceased from night to morning or from day to night without cause. It emphasizes hastening the dead to their graves as part of the Prophetic sunnah (prophetic tradition) and proper communal conduct regarding death.
en.seo_question: Should the burial of the deceased be delayed until morning or night in Islam?

key_terms.مَضَاجِعِهِمْ: their resting places, meaning their graves
